_doc: The application evaluator runs each case as a baseline/no-skill arm and a with-skill arm, then grades behavior against expected_flags, expected_fix_hints, absent_signals, and the per-case criteria checklist.
subject: Use when reasoning about Test-Driven Development as a design discipline rather than a workflow: the red-green-refactor…

cases.scenario: A user asks: "explain why writing the test first changes the design of the code under test"
cases.context: The agent has access to the test-driven-development skill and must decide whether to use it, apply its procedure, and stay inside its boundaries.
cases.question: What should the agent do, and why is test-driven-development the right skill to apply?
expected_flags: Recognizes test-driven-development as applicable to this request
Uses the skill-specific purpose or mental model instead of generic advice
Names the relevant boundary against eval-driven-development, type-safety, testing-strategy
Turns the request into concrete steps, checks, or decisions from the skill
expected_fix_hints: Apply the test-driven-development workflow to the concrete scenario
State the next action and the evidence or verification needed
Call out any adjacent skill that should own a different part of the request
absent_signals: Does not answer with generic advice that could ignore test-driven-development
Does not route to eval-driven-development, type-safety, testing-strategy when the test-driven-development scope is the owner
